title: Sell Mineral Rights in Kim, CO
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Kim, CO | Raton Basin CBM Owner Guide
metaDescription: Hold minerals under ranchland near Kim, CO? We evaluate Raton Basin coalbed methane production off the Vermejo/Raton coals and quote against real decline data.
heroLead: Kim sits over the southern edge of the Raton Basin, where coalbed methane wells have quietly produced gas out of the Vermejo and Raton formation coals since the 1990s.
intro: Kim is remote Las Animas County ranch country close to the New Mexico line, and most mineral owners here inherited a fractional interest from a homestead or grazing allotment rather than bought into a play. Raton Basin CBM wells around Kim were drilled in waves — an initial push in the 1990s, another in the mid-2000s — and a lot of that early production has now settled into long, low, steady output that pays modestly but reliably.

sections.heading: Coalbed methane behaves differently than shale gas
paragraphs: Unlike Niobrara horizontals with a sharp early peak, CBM wells here typically ramp up slowly as water is pumped off the coal seam to release gas, then hold a flatter production curve for years. That means a Kim-area interest tied to an older CBM well may carry a more predictable royalty history than DJ Basin acreage, which matters when we're building a valuation off actual paid volumes instead of a projection.

sections.heading: Produced water and legacy operators
paragraphs: Raton Basin CBM development came with heavy produced-water handling, and some of the original operators from the 1990s boom have sold or merged their Las Animas County assets since. If your division order names a company that no longer exists, that's normal here — we trace the current operator of record through Colorado Oil and Gas Conservation Commission filings before we quote anything.

sections.heading: What your interest is likely worth
paragraphs: Value depends on how much of the original coal seam gas has already been produced and how the well is declining now. Mature CBM wells with 20-plus years of history give us a clean decline trend to work from; newer or shut-in wells take more digging. Either way we hedge our number to recent royalty activity rather than quoting a flat per-acre figure.

faqs.question: Is coalbed methane the same as regular natural gas?
faqs.answer: Chemically similar, but it's produced from coal seams rather than shale or sandstone, and the well behavior — slow ramp-up, long flat tail — is different, which affects how we value the interest.

faqs.question: My division order lists a company I've never heard of. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: No. Several original Raton Basin CBM operators sold their Las Animas County assets years ago. We verify the current operator of record before quoting.

faqs.question: How do I find my legal description if I've lost the deed?
faqs.answer: The Las Animas County clerk and recorder's office can pull it from your grantor's name or a prior deed reference. We can help point you to the right filing once you give us what you have.
